rule: ruling:sam-2026-10-07 claims 8 and 10: the prototype wins by default, and a real constraint it cannot express (persistence, authentication) overrides only as far as the constraint needs; the prototype keeps each user's saved templates to that user alone under 'My templates', so persisting them keeps them private to the signed-in user who saved them.
outcome: A saved template is private to the signed-in user who saved it, stored against their user id and organisation, and listed under 'My templates'; nobody else sees, uses, changes or deletes it. The prototype wins by default and already keeps saved templates to the user who made them (held in their own session, never shared between users, under a 'My templates' heading); real persistence and sign-in only replace the session with a store keyed to that user, so nothing is left for a person to decide.
